subject.title: Feature request: first-class async result routing back to originating topic sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class async route registry in core, expose only the missing plugin/API seams, or leave this as workspace/plugin-owned composition over existing hooks and targeted wake?
rationale: The current code has the lower-level primitives, but the requested registry would define new product policy, storage, privacy, and safety semantics across gateway, sessions, channels, and plugins.

options.title: Plugin/API contract first
options.body: Design the smallest shared API and plugin seams needed for route registration, matching, dedupe, summaries, wake, and approval-gated actions before adding a core registry.

options.title: Core Gateway registry
options.body: Accept a larger core feature that owns SQLite-backed route lifecycle, matching, ambiguity handling, policy, and visible delivery semantics.

options.title: Workspace/plugin-owned only
options.body: Decline core work for now and document how to compose hooks, task delivery, persistent dedupe, and targeted wake in a plugin or local workflow.

recommendation.title: Plugin/API contract first
recommendation.body: Design the smallest shared API and plugin seams needed for route registration, matching, dedupe, summaries, wake, and approval-gated actions before adding a core registry.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core architecture, gateway wake/session routing, and plugin boundaries, and steipete appears in recent routing merge history for the adjacent wake work.
